api_key.instructions: Sign in to the [AgentMail Console](https://console.agentmail.to), open **API Keys** in the left sidebar, click **Create New API Key**, name it, and copy it now (shown once). An org-level key can list inboxes; a pod- or inbox-scoped key limits access to that pod/inbox.
api_key.notes: Console root given; the API Keys page is a sidebar item with no documented deep link.

api_key.instructions: In the Algolia dashboard open **Settings → API Keys**. Copy the **Application ID**, then under **All API Keys** click **New API Key** and grant only the `listIndexes` ACL (add `search` if needed). Copy the key.
api_key.notes: Requests also need header X-Algolia-Application-Id: {application_id}; hosts are per-application. probe_status taken on latency-dsn.algolia.net without a key.

api_key.instructions: Open [Claude Console → API keys](https://platform.claude.com/settings/keys), click **Create Key**, pick the workspace, name it, and copy the key (shown once).
api_key.notes: Also send anthropic-version: 2023-06-01. Authorization: Bearer <key> is now also accepted; x-api-key is the long-standing header. Multi-workspace keys need anthropic-workspace-id.

api_key.instructions: Sign in to the [AssemblyAI dashboard → API Keys](https://www.assemblyai.com/app/api-keys), click **Create new API key** (or copy the default), and store it.
api_key.notes: Raw key in Authorization (no Bearer). EU data residency uses api.eu.assemblyai.com.

api_key.instructions: Sign in to BambooHR, click your name/avatar and choose **API Keys** (or **Settings → Account → API Keys**), click **Add New Key**, name it and copy it (shown once). The key inherits your user's permissions.
api_key.notes: HTTP Basic: API key as username, any string (e.g. 'x') as password. {company_domain} is the subdomain of the login URL. Send Accept: application/json.

api_key.instructions: In beehiiv go to **Settings → Workspace Settings → API** (Owner or Admin role required), click **Create New API Key**, optionally restrict it to one publication, and copy it (shown once).
In Brevo open your profile → **SMTP & API → API Keys**, click **Generate a new API key**, name it and copy it (shown once).
In Buildkite open **Personal Settings → API Access Tokens**, click **New API Access Token**, pick the organization, tick only **read_user** (plus read scopes you need), and copy it (shown once).
api_key.notes: GET /v2/user (needs read_user) returns name/email.

api_key.instructions: In Calendly open **Integrations & apps → API and webhooks**, click **Get a token now** / **Generate new token**, name it, and copy the personal access token (shown once).
In CircleCI open **User Settings → Personal API Tokens**, click **Create New Token**, name it and copy it (shown once).

In the [Clerk Dashboard](https://dashboard.clerk.com) pick the application and instance (Development or Production), open **Configure → API Keys**, and copy the **Secret Key** (`sk_test_…` or `sk_live_…`).
api_key.notes: Secret keys are sk_test_ (development) or sk_live_ (production). /v1/instance returns the current instance; /v1/users?limit=1 is an alternative.

api_key.instructions: In ClickUp click your avatar → **Settings → Apps**, then under **API Token** click **Generate** (or **Regenerate**) and copy the personal token.
api_key.notes: Raw token in Authorization (no Bearer). Unauthenticated probe returns 400; an invalid token returns 401.

api_key.instructions: Open [Cloudflare → My Profile → API Tokens](https://dash.cloudflare.com/profile/api-tokens), click **Create Token → Custom token**, grant **Zone → SSL and Certificates → Edit** for the needed zones, and copy it. Legacy Origin CA keys are deprecated.
api_key.notes: Origin CA keys (header X-Auth-User-Service-Key, prefix v1.0-) are deprecated and removed on 2026-09-30; this entry describes the replacement API token. Unauth probe gives 400 (bad header); verify returns result.status 'active' for a good token. Listing origin certs needs GET /certificates?zone_id=….

api_key.instructions: Open the [Cohere dashboard → API Keys](https://dashboard.cohere.com/api-keys), click **New Trial Key** or **New Production Key**, name it and copy it.

In Contentful open your avatar → **Account settings → CMA tokens** (or Space settings → API keys → Content management tokens), click **Create personal access token**, set an expiry, and copy it (shown once).
In Crowdin open **Account Settings → API**, click **New Token**, name it, tick only the scopes you need (e.g. read-only **Projects**), and copy the token (shown once).
api_key.notes: Crowdin Enterprise uses https://{organization}.api.crowdin.com/api/v2 instead.

api_key.instructions: In Datadog open **Organization Settings → API Keys**, click **New Key**, name it and copy it. Use the host for your site (e.g. api.datadoghq.eu, api.us5.datadoghq.com).
api_key.notes: /api/v1/validate returns {"valid":true} with only DD-API-KEY. Most read endpoints also need DD-APPLICATION-KEY. Host differs by site (US1, US3, US5, EU, AP1, GOV).

api_key.instructions: Sign in to the [Deepgram Console](https://console.deepgram.com/), choose your project, open **API Keys**, click **Create a New API Key**, pick the **Member** role, and copy the key (shown once).
api_key.notes: Header value is 'Token <key>'. Bearer is used only for short-lived JWTs.

api_key.instructions: Open the [DeepSeek Platform → API keys](https://platform.deepseek.com/api_keys), click **Create new API key**, name it and copy it (shown once).
api_key.notes: GET https://api.deepseek.com/models is an equivalent check.

api_key.instructions: In DigitalOcean open **API → Tokens**, click **Generate New Token**, name it, set an expiry, choose **Custom Scopes** with **account:read**, and copy it (shown once).
In Doppler open **Settings → Tokens → Personal** and click **Generate** (or use a project's **Access → Service Tokens** with read access for one config). Copy the token (shown once).
api_key.notes: Prefixes: dp.pt. personal, dp.st. service, dp.sa. service account, dp.ct. CLI. /v3/me returns name, type and workplace. The Tokens page path includes the workplace id, so key_url is the dashboard root.

api_key.instructions: In Dovetail open **Settings → Account** (your personal settings), find **Personal API keys**, click **Create new key**, and copy it (shown once). Keys expire after 30 days.
In ElevenLabs open **Settings → API Keys** (Developers → API Keys), click **Create API Key**, restrict it and enable **User: Read** (plus whatever else you need), and copy it (shown once).
api_key.notes: Restricted keys fail /v1/user without the User read permission. /v1/models answered 404 unauthenticated so it was not chosen.

api_key.instructions: Open the [Exa dashboard → API Keys](https://dashboard.exa.ai/api-keys), click **Create Key**, name it and copy it.
api_key.notes: Authorization: Bearer <key> is also accepted. Search endpoints consume credits; listing websets does not. Team-management endpoints need a separate service key.

api_key.instructions: In Fathom open **Settings → API Access**, click **Generate API Key**, and copy it. The key can read only meetings you recorded or that were shared with you or your team.
Sign in to [Firecrawl → API Keys](https://www.firecrawl.dev/app/api-keys), click **Create API key** (or copy the default key).
Open [Fireworks → Settings → API Keys](https://app.fireworks.ai/settings/users/api-keys), click **Create API Key**, name it and copy it (shown once).
api_key.notes: Unauthenticated probe of /inference/v1/models answered 401. Older keys may not carry the fw_ prefix.

api_key.instructions: Open [Google AI Studio → Get API key](https://aistudio.google.com/app/apikey), click **Create API key**, pick or create a Google Cloud project, and copy the key.
In GitLab open **Avatar → Edit profile → Access tokens**, click **Add new token**, set a name and expiry, tick only **read_user** (add **read_api** if needed), and copy the token (shown once).
api_key.notes: PRIVATE-TOKEN: <token> header is equivalent to Authorization: Bearer. Self-managed instances use their own host.

api_key.instructions: Open [GroqCloud → API Keys](https://console.groq.com/keys), click **Create API Key**, name it and copy it (shown once).

Open [Hugging Face → Access Tokens](https://huggingface.co/settings/tokens), click **Create new token**, choose **Fine-grained** and tick **Make calls to Inference Providers** (or **Read**), and copy it.
Sign in to the [TypeSafe console](https://console.typesafe.ai/settings/keys), open **Settings → API Keys**, click **Create key**, and copy it (shown once).
api_key.notes: Official reference documents only POST /v1/systemone; GET /v1/models as a key check comes from third-party guides (unauth probe answered 403 'Must supply an API key'). TypeSafe paused new signups around 2026-09-22.

api_key.instructions: Sign in to the [Kernel dashboard](https://dashboard.onkernel.com/), open **API Keys**, click **Create API key** (optionally scoped to one project), and copy it (shown once).
api_key.notes: auth.md suggests GET /org/api_keys?limit=1 as the harmless check; /browsers (list) works for project-scoped keys too.

api_key.instructions: In LaunchDarkly open **Organization settings → Authorization**, under **Access tokens** click **Create token**, name it, pick the **Reader** role, and copy it (shown once).
api_key.notes: Raw token in Authorization (no Bearer). caller-identity returns accountId, tokenName, tokenKind.

api_key.instructions: Lemma keys are not self-service: they are issued by the Lemma team during platform onboarding (contact contact@getlemma.com). Paste the key you were given.
api_key.notes: No dashboard page exists, so key_url points at the auth docs. Prefix inferred from the docs' example (lm_key_…). List-entities path inferred from the reference index; /v0/accounts also answers 401.

api_key.instructions: In Linear open **Settings → Account → Security & access**, under **Personal API keys** click **New API key**, name it, choose **Read** access, and copy it (shown once).
api_key.notes: GraphQL: POST with Content-Type: application/json and the read-only viewer query in verify.body. Personal keys go in Authorization raw (no Bearer).

api_key.instructions: Sign in to [Lithic](https://app.lithic.com/settings) and copy the API key from **Settings** (Sandbox key by default; a Production key appears once production is enabled).
api_key.notes: Raw key in Authorization. Sandbox keys work only against https://sandbox.lithic.com/v1.

api_key.instructions: In Mailgun open **Settings → API Security**, click **Add new key**, name it, and copy the private API key (shown once). EU accounts use api.eu.mailgun.net.
api_key.notes: HTTP Basic with username 'api' and the API key as password.

api_key.instructions: Sign in to the [Marqeta developer dashboard](https://app.marqeta.com/development); your sandbox **Application token** and **Admin access token** are shown there. Production credentials come from Marqeta.
api_key.notes: HTTP Basic: application token as username, admin access token as password. Production hosts are program-specific.

api_key.instructions: In the MessageBird dashboard open **Developers → API access**, click **Add access key**, choose **Live** (or **Test**), and copy it.
api_key.notes: Header is 'Authorization: AccessKey <key>' — scheme 'AccessKey' is outside the Bearer/Basic/Token set. Test keys start with test_, live keys have no prefix. MessageBird is now Bird; this is the legacy REST API.

api_key.instructions: Open [Mistral console → API Keys](https://console.mistral.ai/api-keys), click **Create new key**, pick the workspace, set an expiry, and copy it (shown once).
In monday.com click your avatar → **Developers**, then **API token → Show** (admins: **Administration → Connections → Personal API token**) and copy the personal token.
api_key.notes: GraphQL POST, token raw in Authorization. The tokens page lives under your account subdomain (https://{account}.monday.com/apps/manage/tokens).

api_key.instructions: In your n8n instance open **Settings → n8n API**, click **Create an API key**, set a label and expiry (enterprise: pick only `workflow:list`/read scopes), and copy it. Not available on the free trial.
api_key.notes: Instance-specific host (n8n Cloud or self-hosted https://<host>/api/v1). Keys are JWTs.

api_key.instructions: In the Neon Console open your avatar → **Account settings → API keys**, click **Create new API key**, name it and copy it (shown once).
api_key.notes: /users/me works for personal keys; organization keys cannot call it (use GET /api/v2/projects?org_id=… instead).

api_key.instructions: Register at [newsapi.org](https://newsapi.org/register); your API key is shown on the [Account](https://newsapi.org/account) page.
Open [ngrok dashboard → API Keys](https://dashboard.ngrok.com/api-keys), click **New API Key**, add a description, and copy it (shown once). This is not the agent authtoken.
api_key.notes: Also send Ngrok-Version: 2.

api_key.instructions: Open [Notion → Integrations](https://www.notion.so/profile/integrations), click **New integration**, pick the workspace, choose **Internal**, enable **Read content** only, save, and copy the **Internal Integration Secret**. Share pages with it via ••• → Connections.
api_key.notes: Also send Notion-Version: 2022-06-28. Older secrets start with secret_.

api_key.instructions: On npmjs.com click your avatar → **Access Tokens → Generate New Token → Granular Access Token**, set an expiry, choose **Read-only** for packages, and copy the token (shown once).
api_key.notes: key_url uses ~ for the signed-in user (https://www.npmjs.com/settings/<username>/tokens).

api_key.instructions: Open [OpenAI Platform → API keys](https://platform.openai.com/api-keys), click **Create new secret key**, pick the project, choose **Restricted** with **Models: Read** (plus what you need), and copy it (shown once).
Open [OpenRouter → Keys](https://openrouter.ai/settings/keys), click **Create Key**, name it, optionally set a credit limit, and copy it (shown once).
Open the [Perplexity console → API keys](https://console.perplexity.ai/project/keys), click **Create API key**, name it and copy it (shown once). A funded credit balance is needed for paid calls.
api_key.notes: GET /v1/models is listed in the current reference index; GET /async/chat/completions (list) is an alternative read-only check.

api_key.instructions: In the [Pinecone console](https://app.pinecone.io/) pick the project, open **API keys**, click **Create API key**, choose **ReadOnly** (or **All**) permissions, and copy it (shown once).
api_key.notes: Send X-Pinecone-API-Version (e.g. 2025-04). key_url is the console root; API keys live under the project.

api_key.instructions: In Postmark open **Servers**, pick the server, go to **API Tokens**, and copy the **Server API token** (or click **Generate another token**).
api_key.notes: Send Accept: application/json. Account-level tokens use X-Postmark-Account-Token instead.

api_key.instructions: Sign in to [Privacy.com](https://app.privacy.com/account), open **Account**, scroll to **API Key**, and copy (or regenerate) the key. Write access requires an Issuing key from api@privacy.com; reading cards does not.
api_key.notes: Header is 'Authorization: api-key <key>' — scheme 'api-key' is outside the Bearer/Basic/Token set. No header → 403 (nginx); a bad key → 401. Sandbox: sandbox.privacy.com.

api_key.instructions: Open [Railway → Account → Tokens](https://railway.com/account/tokens), create a token with **No workspace** selected (an account token), name it, and copy it.
api_key.notes: A bad token returns HTTP 200 with errors[].message 'Not Authorized' and data null, so check the body. `me` works only with account tokens; workspace tokens need query { workspace(workspaceId:…) { name } }; project tokens use the Project-Access-Token header.

api_key.instructions: In the Render Dashboard open **Account Settings**, scroll to **API Keys**, click **Create API Key**, name it and copy it (shown once). Keys reach every workspace you belong to.
api_key.notes: GET /v1/owners (workspaces) is an alternative check.

api_key.instructions: Open [Replicate → API tokens](https://replicate.com/account/api-tokens), enter a name, click **Create token**, and copy it.
Open [Resend → API Keys](https://resend.com/api-keys), click **Create API Key**, name it, choose **Full access** (a **Sending access** key cannot list domains), and copy it (shown once).
api_key.notes: Sending-only keys return 401 restricted_api_key on /domains; they can only POST /emails.

api_key.instructions: At [sanity.io/manage](https://www.sanity.io/manage) pick the project, open **API → Tokens**, click **Add API token**, name it, choose **Viewer** permissions and an expiry, and copy it (shown once).
api_key.notes: Without any token /users/me answers 200 {} (anonymous); an invalid token answers 401 'Session not found'. Treat an empty body as failure.

api_key.instructions: In Segment open **Settings → Access Management → Tokens**, click **Create Token**, choose **Public API** (not Config API), grant **Workspace Member** with read-only access, and copy it.
api_key.notes: api.segment.io (tracking) takes a source write key via Basic and has no read-only check; this entry uses the Public API token instead. EU workspaces use eu1.api.segmentapis.com.

api_key.instructions: In SendGrid open **Settings → API Keys**, click **Create API Key**, name it, choose **Restricted Access** and only the permissions you need, and copy it (shown once).
api_key.notes: /v3/scopes works for any valid key regardless of its permissions.

api_key.instructions: Sign in to [Stability AI → Account → API Keys](https://platform.stability.ai/account/keys), click **Create API Key** (or copy the existing one).

In the Stripe Dashboard open **Developers → API keys**, click **Create restricted key**, set **Issuing Cards** and **Issuing Cardholders** to **Read**, leave the rest **None**, and copy it (`rk_live_…`/`rk_test_…`).
api_key.notes: Secret keys (sk_) also work; restricted keys (rk_) are least privilege. Issuing must be enabled on the account.

api_key.instructions: Open [@BotFather](https://t.me/BotFather) in Telegram, send `/newbot`, choose a name and a username ending in `bot`, and copy the token it replies with (`123456789:AA…`).
api_key.notes: The token goes in the URL path (bot<token>), not a header.

api_key.instructions: In [Tinybird Cloud](https://cloud.tinybird.co) open your workspace → **Tokens**, click **Create Token**, give it read scope on a data source or pipe, and copy it. Use the API host of your workspace's region.
api_key.notes: Host depends on region (e.g. api.us-east.aws.tinybird.co). key_url is approximate; tokens live under the workspace.

api_key.instructions: Open [Together AI → Settings → API Keys](https://api.together.ai/settings/api-keys), click **Create API key** (or copy the default), and store it.
api_key.notes: Newer keys may start with tgp_v1_; older keys have no fixed prefix, so key_prefix is null.

api_key.instructions: Open [Typeform → Personal tokens](https://admin.typeform.com/user/tokens), click **Generate a new token**, name it, select only **accounts:read**, and copy it (shown once).
api_key.notes: EU data-center accounts use api.eu.typeform.com.

api_key.instructions: Open [Vercel → Account Settings → Tokens](https://vercel.com/account/settings/tokens), enter a name, choose the scope (team) and an expiration, click **Create**, and copy the token (shown once).
api_key.notes: Team resources need ?teamId=… on requests.

api_key.instructions: In Webflow open the site's **Site settings → Apps & integrations → API access**, click **Generate API token**, name it, set **Sites: Read-only** (add others as needed), and copy it (shown once).
api_key.notes: Site tokens are per site; key_url is the dashboard because the settings path contains the site slug.
